copy.headline: Cyber incident hits work on tunnel to Germany; minister summons parties

extended.text: Work on the Femern Belt tunnel, which is to link Rødbyhavn in Denmark with Puttgarden in Germany, has been hit by what the project's website calls a cyber incident. Lisbeth Bech-Nielsen, the minister for public security and preparedness, has summoned the parties behind Denmark's national strategy for cyber and information security to discuss what measures to take.

Bech-Nielsen, of SF, a left-wing party, told TV 2 that 'the serious threat picture and the recent incidents' were the reason. She gave no date and said it was too early to conclude anything, but that 'the authorities are investigating'.

Lolland-Falsters Folketidende, a local newspaper, calls it a hacker attack. It reports that staff were told not to use wi-fi or open computers or emails, that even the guards' access system was down, and that several vessels at sea lay idle because they could not reach digital systems. The trouble began overnight into Monday, it says.
Who is behind it, and when the systems will be back, is not known.
Building began in 2020; the link was first due to open in 2029.

copy.headline: Pope Leo has lung cancer, the Vatican says

standard.text: Pope Leo XIV, the 71-year-old head of the Catholic Church, has lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer, the Vatican said on Tuesday. Surgeons in Rome removed the lower lobe of his right lung in an operation of about an hour and a half, without complications.
He is expected to spend a week in hospital, and his audiences are cancelled until 20 October. He is due to tour Uruguay, Argentina and Peru for 11 days from 6 November.
Further tests are being carried out to see whether the cancer has spread, an unnamed Vatican source told AFP. It is Leo's first serious illness in 17 months as pope.

short.text: Pope Leo XIV, the 71-year-old head of the Catholic Church, has lung cancer, the Vatican said on Tuesday after surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is expected to spend a week in hospital.

copy.headline: Copenhagen flat prices fall for a second month

standard.text: Flat prices in Copenhagen Municipality fell 1.0 per cent from August to September, after a 0.5 per cent fall the month before, according to Boligsiden, a Danish property website. They remain 15.7 per cent higher than a year earlier, at 75,414 kroner per square metre.

Birgit Daetz, a housing economist at Boligsiden, blames more flats for sale this year and weaker demand from buyers. An economist quoted by Politiken expects prices to fall by up to 10 per cent as 2027 begins.
In Aarhus prices rose 3.7 per cent to 50,649 kroner per square metre, the third-largest monthly rise since the figures began in 2011.

short.text: Flat prices in Copenhagen Municipality fell 1.0 per cent in September, the second monthly fall in a row, according to Boligsiden, a Danish property website. In Aarhus they rose 3.7 per cent.

copy.deck: In Aarhus they rose 3.7 per cent and passed 50,000 kroner per square metre for the first time.

copy.headline: Aarhus University apologises for errors behind new nitrogen rules for farmers

standard.text: Aarhus University has apologised for errors in the calculations behind Denmark's new nitrogen rules, which from 1 January 2027 cap how much nitrogen farmers may discharge. The university says it will now gauge the error's extent and correct it; the error matters where much manure is used.

Seges Innovation, a think tank, said last week that some farmers' limits had been set too low. On Friday a government agency said the university had checked the figures and found them in order. A 'triple check' announced on Tuesday found the same error as Seges.
'We did not deliver as we should have, and we deeply regret it,' said Jørgen Eriksen, a professor at the university's Department of Agroecology.

short.text: Aarhus University has apologised for errors in the calculations behind Denmark's new nitrogen rules, which take effect on 1 January 2027. Seges Innovation, a think tank, had flagged the error last week; a government agency said on Friday that the figures were in order.

copy.deck: The university found the error a think tank had flagged, days after its figures were declared in order.

copy.headline: Health authority asks whether suspending three surgeons harms Denmark's only liver-transplant unit

standard.text: Sundhedsstyrelsen, the Danish Health Authority, has asked the Capital Region whether sending home three senior surgeons harms Denmark's only liver-transplant department. The department is at Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen's university hospital. The three were suspended after writing letters of concern to management, according to Sundhedsmonitor, a news outlet, and could be dismissed.

The region had warned the authority in June of surgical problems in its transplant work, Politiken reports. A Norwegian surgeon now assists at liver transplants under a deal with Oslo University Hospital, and from 1 November pancreas patients will be operated on in Norway. Rigshospitalet says the department still has the staff it needs.

short.text: Sundhedsstyrelsen, the Danish Health Authority, has asked the Capital Region whether suspending three senior surgeons harms Denmark's only liver-transplant department, at Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen's university hospital. The three had written letters of concern to management, according to Sundhedsmonitor, a news outlet. The hospital says the department still has the staff it needs.

copy.headline: Sweden's parliament will vote on Magdalena Andersson as prime minister on Thursday

standard.text: The Riksdag, Sweden's parliament, will vote at 12:00 on Thursday on whether Magdalena Andersson, leader of the Social Democrats, should be prime minister of a government of her party alone. Andreas Norlén, the Riksdag's speaker, announced the vote on Tuesday.

Andersson had told him that morning that talks had made progress but that no government the Riksdag would tolerate could yet be formed. If she falls short on Thursday, Norlén will call the other party leaders and speed up the process.
The four red-green parties won 176 seats in the election on 13 September, the centre-right bloc 173.

short.text: The Riksdag, Sweden's parliament, will vote at 12:00 on Thursday on whether Magdalena Andersson, leader of the Social Democrats, should be prime minister of a government of her party alone. She has concluded no government talks with other parties.
